meta.title: Ch 1: Introduction to Indian Accounting Standards — MCQ Bank
meta.description: Chapter-wise practice MCQs for Chapter 1 (Introduction to Indian Accounting Standards).

questions.q: Under the new scheme syllabus, Ind AS are notified under which statutory mechanism?
o: Companies (Indian Accounting Standards) Rules issued by MCA on recommendation of NFRA
Section 129 only of the Companies Act 2013
ICAI issues Ind AS directly as Accounting Standards
SEBI notifies Ind AS for all companies
questions.why: MCA notifies Ind AS through the Companies (Indian Accounting Standards) Rules; the standard-setting process runs through the National Financial Reporting Authority (NFRA), which replaced the earlier AC-AS role. ICAI's role is recommendation/drafting support; SEBI governs listed-company disclosure, not Ind AS notification.
questions.trend: Core concept that appears in some avatar in most attempts under the new scheme (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — governance of standard-setting is a favourite 1-marker AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: Who recommends? NFRA. Who notifies? MCA. Who writes study material? ICAI — three separate chairs; never mix them.

questions.q: As per the roadmap, which class of companies is required to prepare Ind AS-based financial statements for accounting periods beginning on or after 1 April 2018 (in addition to the earlier phases)?
o: All companies listed or intending to list on a stock exchange
All private limited companies with paid-up capital above Rs 100 crore
questions.why: The phased roadmap applied Ind AS from 1.4.2016 to NBFCs, banks, insurers and companies with net worth/turnover above Rs 500 crore; from 1.4.2017 to all companies with net worth/turnover above Rs 250 crore; and from 1.4.2018 to all companies listed or in the process of listing on any stock exchange in India or abroad.
questions.trend: Known trap zone: ICAI objective papers repeatedly test limits/exceptions of this rule (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: HIGH likelihood for Nov 2026 — the roadmap dates are a standing MCQ favourite Prediction is study guidance, not an ICAI statement.

mem.tip: Roadmap ladder: 500 Cr+ and banks/NBFC/insurance from FY17; listed (or going listed) from FY18. Parent/sub follows the parent rule even below limits.

questions.q: Which body now recommends notification of Ind AS accounting standards in the public interest?
questions.why: Under the Companies Act 2013 (as amended), NFRA recommends ICAI to formulate, or recommend for issuance, accounting/auditing standards in the public interest; ICAI continues drafting. MCA notifies.
questions.trend: Core concept that appears in some avatar in most attempts under the new scheme (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — institutional-governance 1-markers recur under the new scheme AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: NFRA recommends, ICAI drafts, MCA notifies — three desks, one assembly line.

questions.q: Under Ind AS, the term used in place of the AS-era 'market value' for most financial-statement purposes is:
questions.why: Ind AS replaced ad-hoc 'market value' usage with the defined exit-price 'fair value' (Ind AS 113).
questions.trend: Core concept that appears in some avatar in most attempts under the new scheme (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — terminology mapping questions open the paper AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.ti: TI: Ind AS vs AS terminology
mem.tip: Fair value is the Ind AS lingua franca; 'market value' is a dead dialect.

questions.q: If an Ind AS requirement conflicts with the Conceptual Framework, the entity follows:
questions.why: The Framework does not override any Ind AS — it guides when a requirement is absent or unclear.
questions.trend: No dominant past-pattern signal; included for balanced coverage (AI judgement).
questions.probWhy: Lower likelihood but possible — supremacy-hierarchy one-liner Included so a low-probability surprise cannot catch you cold.

mem.tip: Standards rule, the Framework fills gaps — never the reverse.

questions.q: A sector regulator (e.g., IRDAI for insurers) may exempt notified companies from specified Ind AS applicability. This exemption comes from:
o: MCA in consultation with the sector regulator, via exemption notifications
questions.why: Under the roadmap, certain classes (banking/insurance/NBFC historically) were deferred/exempted via MCA notifications in consultation with regulators.
questions.trend: No dominant past-pattern signal; included for balanced coverage (AI judgement).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — governance-of-exemptions one-liner AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: The notification door opens only in consultation — never self-certified.

questions.q: Where an Ind AS permits a choice of policy, the selection must be made with reference to:
o: The Framework’s recognition and measurement principles, applied consistently
questions.why: Ind AS 8 requires the chosen policy to give relevant, reliable, comparable information per the Framework — then consistency until a change is required or improves the statements.
questions.trend: Core concept that appears in some avatar in most attempts under the new scheme (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: Lower likelihood but possible — policy-by-principle vs policy-by-convenience is a favourite concept check Included so a low-probability surprise cannot catch you cold.

mem.ti: TI: Ind AS 8 — policy choice anchor
mem.tip: Choices are made by principle, not by convenience — then kept.
